2021_20_2_a_troy_school_district_0621_au.paragraph: Draft Annual Comprehensive Financial Report of Troy School District for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021, transmitted to the Board of Education on October 5, 2021 by Rick West and Kandice Moynihan of Business Services and audited by Plante & Moran, which issued an unmodified opinion. Governmental funds closed the year with a combined fund balance of $57,844,378, while the General Fund balance rose to $32,734,102 in a sixth consecutive year of additions, with unassigned fund balance at 19.98 percent of 2021 general operating expenditures. Districtwide net position was $(201,057,958), weighed down by a $308,094,061 net pension liability and a $48,088,931 net OPEB liability.
2021_20_2_a_troy_school_district_0621_au.page:
**What it is.** Draft Annual Comprehensive Financial Report with supplemental information for Troy School District (Administration Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098) covering the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021. The letter of transmittal is dated October 5, 2021 and signed by Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, and Kandice Moynihan, Director of Finance, Business Services. Plante & Moran was appointed by the Troy Board of Education to audit 2020-21; the opinion is unmodified and there were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards. Board of Education members listed: Karl Schmidt (President), Dr. Nicole Wilson (Vice President), Gary Hauff (Secretary), and trustees Vital Anne, Steve Gottlieb, Elizabeth Hammond and Dr. Nancy Philippart. Superintendent: Richard Machesky, Ed.D.

**Government-wide position, June 30, 2021.**

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Total assets | $283,253,146 |
| Deferred outflows of resources | $93,398,741 |
| Total liabilities | $528,864,531 |
| Deferred inflows of resources | $48,845,314 |
| Net investment in capital assets | $82,174,848 |
| Unrestricted net position | $(284,037,913) |
| Total net position | $(201,057,958) |

Total expenses were $203,874,829 against charges for services of $1,802,535, operating grants and contributions of $52,855,894, and general revenue of $144,318,096, producing a change in net position of $(4,898,304) from a beginning balance of $(196,159,654). MD&A attributes the reduction primarily to the net decrease in deferred pension and OPEB costs.

**Governmental funds.** Combined fund balance was $57,844,378, described in MD&A as a decrease of $6.2 million from the prior year. Total revenue was $201,492,650 and total expenditures $206,573,406. The General Fund reported revenue of $171,189,282, expenditures of $164,655,892, a net change in fund balance of $6,724,392, and an ending balance of $32,734,102 (unassigned $31,807,875). The 2019 Capital Projects Fund ended at $18,231,222 after $8,487,133 of capital outlay; nonmajor funds ended at $6,879,054, including a Sinking Fund balance of $2,731,074 and a Capital Maintenance Fund balance of $680,536.

**General Fund budget versus actual.**

| Line | Original | Final | Actual |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total revenue | $149,632,442 | $171,367,704 | $171,189,282 |
| Total expenditures | $161,272,639 | $165,691,478 | $164,655,892 |
| Net change in fund balance | $(10,215,197) | $5,865,626 | $6,724,392 |
| Ending fund balance | $15,794,513 | $31,875,336 | $32,734,102 |

The original budget assumed a $700 per pupil foundation reduction; the final budget reflected a flat foundation allowance of $9,315 per pupil plus a one-time $65 per pupil increase.

**Debt.** General obligation bonds outstanding fell to $130,280,000 from $140,565,000, with unamortized premium of $7,678,963. During the year the district issued $40,425,000 of refunding bonds at 0.20 to 1.56 percent and advance refunded $37,860,000 of 2012 and 2014 debt. Remaining principal and interest to maturity total $155,626,003. S&P affirmed the AA/Stable rating in May 2021.

**Pensions and OPEB (MPSERS).** Net pension liability $308,094,061 and net OPEB liability $48,088,931, both measured at September 30, 2020. Pension expense was $47,852,726; the district recognized an OPEB recovery of $860,940. Actual pension contributions were $27,611,786 and OPEB contributions $6,980,805.

**District profile.** Enrollment of 12,723 as of Spring 2021 across 12 elementary schools, four middle schools, two comprehensive high schools, an International Baccalaureate Academy, an alternative high school, and Intersect; 448.74 acres and 2,185,181 square feet of buildings; 985 full-time equivalent employees; 71 buses; average teacher salary $75,918.
2021_20_2_a_troy_school_district_0621_au.verbose:
Draft Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) with supplemental information for Troy School District, a school district in the State of Michigan, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021, presented to the Board of Education at the October 5, 2021 meeting. The letter of transmittal, dated October 5, 2021 and addressed to the Citizens of Troy and the Board Members, is signed by Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services (4400 Livernois, 248.823.4022, rwest@troy.k12.mi.us) and Kandice Moynihan, Director of Finance, Business Services. The Administration Building is at 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, phone (248) 823-4000, fax (248) 823-4013.

**Officials.** Board of Education: Karl Schmidt, President; Dr. Nicole Wilson, Vice President; Gary Hauff, Secretary; Vital Anne, Trustee; Steve Gottlieb, Trustee; Elizabeth Hammond, Trustee; Dr. Nancy Philippart, Trustee. Administration: Richard Machesky, Ed.D., Superintendent; Rick West, Assistant Superintendent Business Services; Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent Secondary Instruction; Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent Employee Services; Kristine Griffor, Assistant Superintendent Elementary Instruction; Kerry Birmingham, Director of Communications and Strategic Initiatives.

**Audit.** Plante & Moran was appointed by the Troy Board of Education to perform the 2020-21 audit and issued an unmodified opinion dated October 5, 2021, the same date as the Government Auditing Standards internal control report and the subsequent-events evaluation date. There were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards for the year ended June 30, 2021. ASBO awarded Certificates of Excellence in Financial Reporting for fiscal years ended June 30, 1989-2019.

**District profile.** Enrollment as of Spring 2021 was 12,723 students in kindergarten through twelfth grade in 20 schools, plus students with developmental disabilities ages 19-26 in the Troy Center for Transition/Grow Program. The configuration is 12 elementary schools, four middle schools, two comprehensive college-preparatory high schools, one International Baccalaureate Academy, one alternative high school, and Intersect, the online homeschool partnership. Students speak more than 80 languages at home. The City of Troy covers 26.61 square miles, is the largest city in Oakland County and the 13th largest in Michigan, with a population of 85,584, more than 6,000 businesses with a market value over $12 billion, and more than 57 percent of residents holding a bachelor's degree or higher. Eighteen buildings hold state exemplary recognition, and eight have National Blue Ribbon awards (Bemis, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wattles, Larson, Athens, Troy High, International Academy). The building inventory totals 448.74 acres and 2,185,181 square feet, led by Athens High School (398,426 sq ft, 1974, 1,579 students), Troy High School (343,207, 1992, 2,100), International Academy East (81,455, 571), Troy College and Career High School (37,520, 212), Baker (694), Boulan (844), Larson (733) and Smith (628), plus the 2019 Preschool (72,000 sq ft, 108) and the Troy Center for Transitions (59).

**COVID-19 and federal relief.** Approximately $6.9 million of CRF and ESSER I funds were received and spent in 2020-2021 on technology equipment, online learning resources and personal protective equipment; ESSER II and ESSER III allocations followed, along with a state equity payment of $385 per pupil and an anticipated further equity payment of more than $900 per pupil in 2021-2022. Standard & Poor's affirmed the AA/Stable rating in May 2021, and a Supervisor of Equity, Inclusion, and Community Engagement was hired in 2020-2021.

**Government-wide statements.** Assets at June 30, 2021 totaled $283,253,146: cash and cash equivalents $24,576,586, other receivables $367,834, due from other governmental units $22,481,914, inventory $126,751, prepaid expenses $131,932, restricted assets $36,391,198, nondepreciable capital assets $3,164,894 and depreciable capital assets net $196,012,037. Deferred outflows totaled $93,398,741 (bond refunding charges $517,860, pension $69,417,209, OPEB $23,463,672). Liabilities totaled $528,864,531, including accounts payable $2,509,401, due to other governmental units $5,299,819, accrued salaries and wages $8,951,060, payroll taxes and withholdings $6,403,279, accrued interest $606,366, unearned revenue $3,068,278, noncurrent liabilities due within one year $15,588,619 and thereafter $130,254,717, net pension liability $308,094,061 and net OPEB liability $48,088,931. Deferred inflows totaled $48,845,314 (pension contribution support $11,658,202, pension cost reductions $1,056,476, OPEB cost reductions $36,130,636). Net position: net investment in capital assets $82,174,848, restricted for capital projects $523,276 and food service $281,831, unrestricted $(284,037,913), total $(201,057,958).

Statement of activities expenses were instruction $120,915,752, support services $67,702,339, athletics $1,700,708, food services $2,416,697, community services $6,324,376, interest $4,533,849 and other debt costs $281,108, totaling $203,874,829, offset by charges for services of $1,802,535 and operating grants of $52,855,894 for net expense of $(149,216,400). General revenue of $144,318,096 includes property taxes levied for general purposes $39,308,501, debt service $17,345,162 and capital projects $4,152,751; unrestricted state aid $81,687,900; unrestricted federal grants $23,088; interest and investment earnings $97,442; loss on disposal of capital assets $(708,156); student activities $1,186,381; and other $1,225,027.

**Fund statements.** Governmental fund revenue of $201,492,650 comprised local sources $65,117,799, state sources $110,743,625, federal sources $15,532,995 and interdistrict sources $10,098,231. Expenditures of $206,573,406 comprised instruction $110,296,670, support services $51,263,342, athletics $1,593,596, food services $2,355,746, community services $3,400,743, debt principal $12,850,000, interest $5,517,016, other debt costs $281,108, and capital outlay $19,015,185. Other financing sources and uses included face value of debt issued $40,425,000, transfers in and out of $1,847,391, and a payment to the bond refunding escrow agent of $(41,571,042), for a net change in fund balances of $(6,217,397) from a beginning combined balance of $64,061,775 to $57,844,378. General Fund detail: revenue $171,189,282, expenditures $164,655,892, excess of revenue over expenditures $6,533,390, ending fund balance $32,734,102 (nonspendable inventory $87,927 and prepaids $131,932; assigned for subsequent year's budget $706,368; unassigned $31,807,875). MD&A puts the unassigned fund balance at 19.98 percent of 2021 general operating expenditures, the sixth consecutive year of additions, against a 15 percent policy minimum. Special revenue balances rose from $2.8 million to $3.1 million; debt service balances fell $1.2 million with the debt millage unchanged at 4.10 mills; capital project balances fell $12.1 million; sinking fund collections were $4.1 million. Custodial funds held $109,854 in cash and $2,057 of payables, ending at $107,797 after additions of $127,342 and deductions of $133,591.

**Budget.** The final General Fund amendment was adopted in June 2021, raising budgeted revenue $20.5 million: state sources up $14.8 million (no per pupil reduction; foundation allowance flat at $9,315 plus a one-time $65 per pupil increase), federal up $6.8 million (largely $6.7 million of CARES Act Coronavirus Relief Funds), interdistrict up $1.0 million on PA18 millage, and $1.4 million of property-sale revenue removed. Budget-to-actual: revenue original $149,632,442, final $171,367,704, actual $171,189,282; expenditures original $161,272,639, final $165,691,478, actual $164,655,892; ending fund balance original $15,794,513, final $31,875,336, actual $32,734,102, a favorable variance of $858,766. Largest actual functions were basic programs $87,483,395, added needs $21,334,681, pupil support $11,914,484, operations and maintenance $11,570,833, instructional staff $10,807,305 and school administration $9,005,170.

**Capital assets and debt.** Capital assets totaled $392,874,746 less accumulated depreciation of $193,697,815 for a net $199,176,931, against $197,066,547 in 2020: land $2,086,043, construction in progress $1,078,851, buildings and improvements $339,039,052, furniture and equipment $50,670,800. Additions were $10,789,342 and depreciation expense $9,040,252 (support services $6,088,627, community services $2,636,613, instruction $265,662, food services $48,017, athletics $1,333). Construction commitments left $1,018,395 remaining on Sinking Fund work ($686,281 spent) and $1,779,974 on other projects ($280,970 spent). General obligation bonds outstanding were $130,280,000 versus $140,565,000, with bond premium of $7,678,963, total bonds payable $137,958,963; compensated absences were $7,666,873 and other termination benefits $217,500. Outstanding issues include the $43,580,000 2012 refunding bond (1.89 percent, maturing May 1, 2022, $4,160,000 outstanding), the $52,710,000 2014 bond (5.00 percent, 2023, $4,000,000), the $31,930,000 2015 refunding bond (5.00 percent, 2026, $16,200,000), the $40,000,000 2016 bond (2.94-4.50 percent, 2032, $32,900,000), the $7,125,000 2018 bond (3.00-3.75 percent, 2040, $6,870,000), the $22,630,000 2019 bond (5.00 percent, 2034, $19,975,000), the $6,100,000 2020 bond (2.00 percent, 2035, $5,750,000), the $7,110,000 2021 refunding bond (0.20-0.30 percent, 2023) and the $33,315,000 2021 refunding bond (0.30-1.56 percent, 2028). Debt service to maturity totals $130,280,000 principal and $25,346,003 interest, or $155,626,003. The advance refunding issued $40,425,000 to refund $37,860,000 of 2012 and 2014 debt; after $278,958 of underwriting fees, insurance and issuance costs plus $1,425,000 of Debt Fund monies, securities were placed in an irrevocable escrow, cutting debt service over the next 7 years by approximately $4,064,000 for an economic gain the report prints as approximately $2.559,000. MD&A cites a statutory debt limit of $613.8 million; the statistical section shows a 2021 legal debt margin of $505,078,261 against a limit of $635,014,922 and net debt subject to limit of $129,936,661 (20.46 percent).

**MPSERS pension and OPEB.** Net pension liability $308,094,061 and net OPEB liability $48,088,931, both measured September 30, 2020 from a September 30, 2019 valuation rolled forward; proportions were 0.90 percent for pension (0.88 percent prior) and 0.90 percent for OPEB (0.89 percent prior). Pension expense was $47,852,726 and OPEB recovery $860,940. Required and actual contributions were $27,611,786 for pension (including $11,658,202 of state UAAL stabilization revenue) and $6,980,805 for OPEB; year-end payables to the plans were $7,516,769 and $951,164. Contribution rate ranges were 13.39-19.78 percent pension and 7.57-8.43 percent OPEB for October 1, 2020 through September 30, 2021. Discount rates were 6.00-6.80 percent for pension and 6.95 percent for OPEB; the healthcare cost trend rate was 7.00 percent in year 1. At a 1 percentage point lower discount rate the net pension liability would be $398,775,499 and at 1 point higher $232,939,362; the net OPEB liability would be $61,775,698 or $36,565,821.

**Other notes and statistics.** The district designated 11 financial institutions and used 2; $41,756,072 of bank deposits were uninsured and uncollateralized; MILAF holdings were $1,219,400 (Cash Management) and $18,258,271 (MAX Class), both rated AAAm by S&P, totaling $19,477,671. Restricted assets of $36,391,198 comprised unspent bond proceeds $19,533,470, unspent sinking fund taxes $3,111,811 and unspent debt service taxes $13,745,917. Unearned revenue of $3,068,278 comprised student lunch accounts $198,128, tuition and fees $429,407 and categorical aid $2,440,743. Operating leases for the Troy Career Center building and a copier fleet cost $122,804 and $89,112, with $246,356 of future minimum payments. Tax abatements under PA 198 of 1974 and brownfield agreements reduced property tax revenue by $114,000, with about $99,000 reimbursed by the State; property and liability risk runs through the SET-SEG shared risk program. Statistical tables show 2020 taxable value of $4,233,432,812 at 23.0826 mills, a levy of $60,779,142 with total collections of $60,806,414 (100.04 percent), Somerset Collections as top taxpayer at $58,558,600, William Beaumont Hospital as top employer with 2,300 employees and the district second with 1,261, 985 full-time equivalent employees, 813 teaching staff, 11.00 percent free/reduced meal eligibility, average teacher salary $75,918, cost per pupil $12,942, revenue per pupil $13,455, and 71 buses. The 2021-2022 budget, adopted June 2021, assumed a $163 per pupil increase to a $9,478 foundation allowance; after year end the School Aid Act was approved and the district expects an additional $171 per pupil compared with 2020-2021.
